title: Mozambique
capsule: The People's Republic of Mozambique (República Popular de Moçambique) became independent from Portugal on 25 June 1975 after a decade of guerrilla war by FRELIMO; the dataset's from-year of 1976 reflects the formal constitutional consolidation under President Samora Machel's one-party Marxist-Leninist state. A devastating civil war against RENAMO, backed by Rhodesia and apartheid South Africa, ravaged the country from 1977 until the General Peace Accord signed in Rome on 4 October 1992, which killed approximately one million people and displaced millions more. Mozambique transitioned to multiparty elections in 1994 — won by Joachim Chissano — and subsequently became one of the world's fastest-growing economies in the 2000s despite recurring cyclones and, after 2017, an Islamist insurgency in Cabo Delgado province.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Modern state boundaries are precisely defined by treaty and UN recognition; internal administrative control varied considerably during the civil war years.
